articles.title: Rupert Murdoch ‘very happy’ that Guy Pearce plays him in Fleet Street biopic Ink
articles.summary: Actor says the press baron’s daughter Elisabeth told him her father was pleased, ‘but he hadn’t seen the film at that point’ Rupert Murdoch is “very happy” that he’s being portrayed by Guy Pearce in a new film about the origins of British tabloid the Sun, the Australian actor has said.
body: Speaking at the Venice film festival ahead of the premiere of 28 Days Later director Danny Boyle’s Ink, Pearce said he had been messaging with the media tycoon’s daughter Elisabeth “and she did say ‘Dad’s very happy that you’re playing him’.”
“But he hadn’t seen the film at that point, so we’ll see,” Pearce added, who had his breakout role in 1994’s The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert.
Ink is set in 1969, the year Murdoch took over the ailing newspaper and installed Larry Lamb (Jack O’Connell) with a mission to outsell the Daily Mirror, then Britain’s leading tabloid.
Playwright James Graham, on whose script the film is based, said Murdoch senior twice visited performances of the stage version in the West End and on Broadway.

articles.title: Mayday review – Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh set cold war bromance alight
articles.summary: An American fighter pilot teams up with a retired KGB officer for hijinks and hilarity in Soviet Russia. Ryan Reynolds and Kenneth Branagh star in this goofy but entertaining action-comedy bromance set in the cold war 80s, when it seemed every red-blooded young guy in America adored Top Gun and…
body: Reynolds is Troy Kelly (callsign “Assassin”), a supercool fighter pilot in 1987, who is always doing brave and brilliant stuff that isn’t in the rulebook, and cracking wise in the accepted Reynolds manner. But when his spy plane is shot down deep inside snowy and forested Soviet territory, Troy awakens from his coma to find himself in the log cabin of retired KGB man Nikolai Ustinov, cheerfully played by Branagh, who is a secret fan of all things American and obsessively rewatches Top Gun on samizdat VHS. He suggests to the stunned Troy that he simply stays in his cabin, watching the film with him, until the cold war is over.

articles.title: ‘He’s a good man’: George Clooney defends Mark Ruffalo in Paramount-Warner Bros merger row
articles.summary: ‘I worry whenever big companies are consolidating,’ Clooney said at Venice film festival, supporting Ruffalo’s right to criticise the deal amid antisemitism accusations.
body: George Clooney has defended Mark Ruffalo’s right to criticise the proposed $111bn Paramount takeover of Warner Bros Discovery, saying he is concerned about the consequences of further consolidation in Hollywood.

Speaking in Venice ahead of receiving the festival’s Golden Lion for lifetime achievement, Clooney said he supported Ruffalo’s “ability to speak freely” about the proposed merger, while expressing his own doubts about the deal.
“I worry when a big company swallows up another company,” Clooney said. “I always worry whenever big companies are consolidating because it means a lot of people are going to lose their jobs.”

Ruffalo has emerged as one of the most outspoken opponents of the Paramount-Warner Bros deal. In a social media post last month, the Marvel star attacked the proposed merger over its potential consequences for Hollywood, while also turning his criticism on the family behind Paramount. David Ellison, the company’s chief executive, is the son of Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, and Ruffalo accused the Ellison family of being complicit the “genocide” of Palestinians, arguing that it was “built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle”.

articles.title: The Eyes Wide Shut conspiracy theory: did someone cut a crucial 20 minutes from Kubrick’s final movie?
articles.summary: For years some have claimed a key part of the thriller was excised after the director’s sudden death – and that it provided clues to the real-life behaviour of rich predators. Now, his daughter has spoken out. Name: The Eyes Wide Shut conspiracy.
body: Age: The erotic psychological thriller Eyes Wide Shut starring Tom Cruise and Nicole Kidman (married at the time, though that isn’t so important now) was released in 1999.
Stanley Kubrick, no? yes. It was the great film-maker’s final movie. He died of a heart attack just days after screening his final cut to Warner Bros. His sudden death is what started it all.
Oooh, go on. OK, so there are rumours that the studio cut 20 minutes of the film after his death, including an alternative ending.

Why would they do that? It was too dark apparently, even by Kubrick’s standards. The theory goes that in Kubrick’s original, Cruise and Kidman’s characters sacrificed their own daughter to a child sexual abuse ring.

articles.title: George Clooney Calls Out ‘Authoritarians’ and ‘People Who Peddle in Fear’ in Moving Venice Golden Lion Speech: They’re ‘Never the Heroes in History’
articles.summary: George Clooney delivered a moving speech about the power of art in times of political turmoil at Venice Film Festival on Wednesday night, saying: “Stories are always dangerous to people who peddle in fear.” The Oscar winner was on hand at the festival’s opening ceremony to accept the Golden Lion…
body: “We’re living through a moment in time where the people in charge and people with the most money are telling us to fear one another,” Clooney said. “But we know better than that, don’t we? Because history does teach us a lesson.”

He continued, “The first people that authoritarians try to shut down are not politicians. They’re journalists who ask questions, they’re the artists who refuse simple answers, the filmmakers, writers, actors and musicians who insist that someone you never met is deserving of your empathy.”
Clooney asserted that “stories are always dangerous to people who peddle in fear” and “the people who are afraid of books and music and stories are never the heroes in history.”

He added, “So yes, movies don’t stop wars, they don’t lower inflation, they don’t fix elections. But they do do something remarkable. They remind us that a stranger is never stranger, and that he might just be the hero in somebody else’s story. And if we can still sit together in the dark and care about people we’ve never met, I think we’ll be OK.”

articles.title: King hails 'unprecedented' Bayeux Tapestry exhibition in London
articles.summary: British and French leaders will be at the British Museum to see the exhibition of the historic Bayeux Tapestry.
body: King Charles has hailed the "unprecedented loan" of the Bayeux Tapestry to the British Museum, calling it the "best possible symbol" of the closeness between the UK and France.

After viewing the medieval tapestry in London on Wednesday a week before it goes on public display, he spoke in French and English to guests including President Emmanuel Macron of France and Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
The King said he was the direct descendant of one of the key figures in the tapestry, William, Duke of Normandy, whose army invaded and defeated King Harold at the Battle of Hastings in 1066.
The tapestry "tells the story of the beginning of what I like to think of as the French side of my family's history in these islands", he added.

articles.title: ‘Ink’ Review: Danny Boyle’s Gripping, Sizzling Film About How a People’s Paper Lost Its Humanity, and Won
articles.summary: “People need stories,” says Larry Lamb, beleaguered editor of leading British tabloid The Sun, at a late point in “Ink,” a propulsive, can’t-look-away account of his simultaneously triumphant and regrettable career zenith.
body: Jack O'Connell is superb as trailblazing tabloid editor Larry Lamb, both in cahoots and at odds with Guy Pearce's Rupert Murdoch, in this tangy Venice opener, adapted from James Graham's play.

But mostly it’s just a very compelling yarn, galvanized by a terrifically bullish performance from Jack O’Connell as Lamb, a Yorkshire-born working-class striver whose populist redirection of the then-struggling paper is presented both as a canny business move and a kind of personal vindication: a poke in the eye of the posh, fusty old boys who had controlled Fleet Street — and thus his career — up to that point. Is it vindication if it costs a man his soul?

articles.title: The Other Bennet Sister wraps filming Christmas special
articles.summary: The producer of the show tells fans online that filming has finished for three special episodes.
body: Filming has wrapped for a three-part Christmas special of hit BBC TV show The Other Bennet Sister, as fans eagerly await its return.

Inspired by Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice, the first series - filmed largely in Wales - attracted 7.3 million UK viewers in its first four weeks, while also having huge success in the US and Canada and on social media.
Welsh actress and creator of Gavin and Stacey, Ruth Jones, portrays the "iconic" Mrs Bennet, with Richard E. Grant playing her husband, Mr Bennet.
On Monday, the show's TV producer Edoardo Ferretti told fans on social media that the special had finished filming.

articles.title: Lizzo 'grateful' after judge dismisses lawsuit against production company
articles.summary: The About Damn Time singer says she is "relieved" at the outcome and will "continue to fight" every claim.
body: US pop star Lizzo has spoken out after the remaining claims in a lawsuit against her production company were thrown out by a US district judge.

The singer's former wardrobe assistant Asha Daniels alleged she had been subjected to "degradation, forced physical labor, denial of medical care, sexual harassment, and racial harassment" while briefly working for Big Grrrl Big Touring in 2023.
In 2024, judge Aenlle-Rocha ruled that Daniels could not sue the Grammy winner as an individual, but Big Grrrl Big Touring Inc remained a defendant.

In his ruling this week, he said the former wardrobe assistant did not identify any conduct by company employees that would demonstrate "general hostility to women in the workplace" or "disparate treatment of men and women".
